namespaceDimensions.label: Address
namespaceDimensions.description: A human-readable identifier that points users and software toward Internet resources.

namespaceDimensions.label: Contract
namespaceDimensions.description: A registration exists through contractual relationships among registrant, registrar and registry.

namespaceDimensions.label: Market
namespaceDimensions.description: Names can have retail prices, premium pricing, renewals and secondary-market value.

namespaceDimensions.label: Jurisdiction
namespaceDimensions.description: Policies, eligibility rules and legal obligations differ across namespaces and operators.

namespaceDimensions.label: Identity
namespaceDimensions.description: A domain can accumulate reputation and become a persistent identifier for an institution, place or person.

namespaceDimensions.label: Trust boundary
namespaceDimensions.description: Some namespaces add verification, security requirements or cryptographic validation around names.

namespaceDimensions.label: Cultural sign
namespaceDimensions.description: Communities and language can give a TLD meanings far beyond its formal designation.

namespaceDimensions.label: Political object
namespaceDimensions.description: Country codes, geographic names and allocation disputes can reflect institutions, borders and public authority.

domainLifecycle.label: Available
domainLifecycle.description: The name is not currently registered and may be eligible under the registry policy.

domainLifecycle.label: Registered
domainLifecycle.description: A registrant enters a registration agreement through a registrar; the registry records the name.

domainLifecycle.label: Renewal loop
domainLifecycle.description: The registration can be renewed for another term under the applicable agreement and policies.

domainLifecycle.label: Expired
domainLifecycle.description: If the registration term ends, post-expiration rules apply; renewal or restoration may still be possible depending on policy and timing.

domainLifecycle.label: Redemption period
domainLifecycle.description: If an applicable gTLD registration is deleted by the registrar, it enters a 30-day redemptionPeriod during which restoration may be possible.

domainLifecycle.label: PendingDelete
domainLifecycle.description: If it is not restored during redemptionPeriod, the name enters pendingDelete for five days and cannot be restored.

domainLifecycle.label: Available again
domainLifecycle.description: After purge from the registry database, the name may become available for registration again under the registry policy.

controlLevers.label: Hosting provider
controlLevers.description: Can remove or disable hosted content or infrastructure it controls.

controlLevers.label: DNS provider
controlLevers.description: Can stop serving authoritative DNS or change resolution for zones it operates.

controlLevers.label: Registrar
controlLevers.description: Maintains the registrant relationship and submits registration changes to the registry.

controlLevers.label: Registry operator
controlLevers.description: Maintains the TLD registry and can add, modify or delete registrations through the registry system under applicable rules.

controlLevers.label: Browser / security layer
controlLevers.description: Can warn, block or distrust destinations independently of the domain registration itself.

controlLevers.label: ICANN
controlLevers.description: Coordinates policies and contracts for gTLDs but is not a general-purpose content regulator or Internet police force.

dnsCapabilities.label: Mail routing
dnsCapabilities.description: MX records direct email toward mail servers for a domain.

dnsCapabilities.label: Email authentication
dnsCapabilities.description: DNS-published policies and keys help receivers evaluate whether mail is authorized and authenticated.

dnsCapabilities.label: Certificate authorization
dnsCapabilities.description: CAA records let a domain indicate which certificate authorities may issue certificates for it.

dnsCapabilities.label: Integrity and origin authentication
dnsCapabilities.description: DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures that allow resolvers to validate DNS data and a chain of trust.

dnsCapabilities.label: Service discovery
dnsCapabilities.description: SRV records can advertise the hostname and port of services associated with a domain.

dnsCapabilities.label: Connection hints
dnsCapabilities.description: SVCB and HTTPS records can publish service endpoints and connection parameters before an application connects.

tldModels.label: General application
tldModels.description: A 2026 application that does not fall into a specialized application type.

tldModels.label: Geographic Name application
tldModels.description: A specialized application for a string that meets the 2026 geographic-name criteria and applicable support or non-objection requirements.

tldModels.label: Reserved Name application
tldModels.description: A specialized application involving a name reserved under the 2026 Applicant Guidebook rules.

tldModels.label: Community Application
tldModels.description: A specialized application linked to a clearly delineated community and the additional commitments required for that designation.

tldModels.label: .Brand TLD application
tldModels.description: A specialized application for an eligible string tied to a registered trademark and its qualifying operator.

tldModels.label: IDN application
tldModels.description: An application for a TLD string represented in a script supported through the Internationalized Domain Name framework.

tldModels.label: Variant string application
tldModels.description: An application involving one or more variant strings evaluated with the primary applied-for string under the 2026 rules.

tldModels.label: Government / IGO application
tldModels.description: An application submitted by a government or intergovernmental organization and treated as a specialized application.

tldModels.label: Applicant Support
tldModels.description: An application from an applicant qualifying for assistance through the Applicant Support Program is treated as specialized.

tldModels.label: Open registration
tldModels.description: A namespace broadly open to eligible registrants under its registry and registrar rules.

tldModels.label: Restricted / verified
tldModels.description: A namespace where eligibility is verified and registration is limited under additional registry policies.

successFramework.label: Scale
successFramework.description: How many names are registered, and how quickly the namespace grows or contracts.

successFramework.label: Active use
successFramework.description: Whether registered names resolve to real services, websites, email or machine-readable endpoints.

successFramework.label: Renewal
successFramework.description: Whether registrants keep names over time rather than treating the namespace as disposable inventory.

successFramework.label: Trust and abuse
successFramework.description: Security controls, abuse rates, verification requirements and the credibility attached to the namespace.

successFramework.label: Diversity
successFramework.description: How registrations are distributed across registrants, registrars, sectors and geographies.

successFramework.label: Purpose fulfilment
successFramework.description: Whether the namespace achieves the mission for which it exists, even if raw registration volume is modest.

successFramework.label: Public value
successFramework.description: For civic namespaces: local adoption, verified actors, useful services, interoperability and measurable public value.
